correctness.rationale: The positive real kernel-overlap constraint forces a-bar b real and the exact hyperbolic parameterization a=(w-k)/(1-kw), k=sqrt(1-q²). Swapping inputs bounds the non-dominant branch. The attained scalar F(w)=qw(1-w²)/D(w), D=1-βw²-(1-β)kw>0, vanishes at 0,1; differentiating yields N=1-(3-β)w²+2(1-β)kw³+βw⁴. N decreases strictly from 1 to -2(1-β)(1-k), giving one root u. N(k)=q²[(2-β)q²-(1-β)] establishes sign geometry; envelope differentiation gives β_c=(1-2q²)/(1-q²) for q<1/sqrt2 and unique q sqrt(1-q²) minimum. Double-root rescaling yields small-q and β→1 expansions; q=1 and β=0 endpoints explicitly covered. Independent 90 parameter/root tests support, but do not replace, these analytic arguments.
residual_risks: Exact boundary statements are for fixed secondary parameters and not uniform at simultaneous q→0, β→1; β=1 excluded.

value.rationale: Optimizing geometric damping at fixed kernel fidelity is a natural compact-operator design question. The exact nonmonotone β phase below q=1/sqrt2, unique optimal damping and antipodal-to-aligned kernel transition solve a structural optimization left open by the published scalar branch representation; asymptotics quantify singular boundaries. The result adds meaningful mathematics beyond the already known circular range.
residual_risks: One previously published numerical example for q=0.5, β=0.5 was inconsistent with independently verified scalar maximization, but this does not prove all earlier numerics erroneous.

limitations: The source disk geometry and scalar maximum are credited to Bhattacharya–Patra. No full claim for β=1.
